<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="מנחם אב_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919915_theRebbe_134" batchId="meluket-_D7_9E_D7_A0_D7_97_D7_9D_20_D7_90_D7_91_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919915_theRebbe_134__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the difference between the encompassing light and the permeating light exists even in their root before the tzimtzum, based on the nature of the light as either for revealing the Essence or for illuminating worlds.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood based on what is explained in the maamar beginning "Zeh" in the series of the year 5672 (1912),</t>
    <t s="2">that the difference between the permeating light and the encompassing light is also in their root before the tzimtzum.</t>
    <t s="3">For that the light of the line</t>
    <t s="4">(the permeating light)</t>
    <t s="5">becomes enclothed in vessels is</t>
    <t s="6">(not only because its drawing down is through the tzimtzum,</t>
    <t s="7">but rather)</t>
    <t s="8">because even in their root before the tzimtzum it is a light that is in the category of limitation</t>
    <t s="9">[for this is that even before the tzimtzum there are the concealed ten sefiros],</t>
    <t s="10">except that before the tzimtzum,</t>
    <t s="11">the limitation within it is in concealment</t>
    <t s="12">(concealed ten sefiros),</t>
    <t s="13">and after the limitation within it is revealed through the tzimtzum,</t>
    <t s="14">it is able to become enclothed in vessels.</t>
    <t s="15">And the reason for this, that this light is in the category of limitation,</t>
    <t s="16">even though the definition of light is that it is attached to the Essence and is of the same kind as the Essence,</t>
    <t s="17">is,</t>
    <t s="18">because the purpose of this light is to illuminate the worlds.</t>
    <t s="19">And this is the difference between the light of "without beginning and without end"</t>
    <t s="20">(the root of the encompassing light)</t>
    <t s="21">and the light that is in the category of limitation</t>
    <t s="22">(the root of the permeating light),</t>
    <t s="23">that the light of "without beginning and without end,"</t>
    <t s="24">it is</t>
    <t s="25">(not in order to illuminate,</t>
    <t s="26">but rather)</t>
    <t s="27">a revelation of the Essence.</t>
    <t s="28">And even though this revelation too is for some purpose</t>
    <t s="29">(for above there is no compulsion, heaven forbid)</t>
    <t s="30">— the purpose in the revelation of this light is that there should be a revelation whose essence is</t>
    <t s="31">(not to illuminate, but rather)</t>
    <t s="32">a revelation of the Essence.</t>
    <t s="33">Therefore,</t>
    <t s="34">in this light it is not applicable that there should be in it measurement and limitation</t>
    <t s="35">(ten sefiros)</t>
    <t s="36">even in concealment,</t>
    <t s="37">and even after it shines into vessels and worlds, it does not come into them in an enclothed manner, but only encompasses them,</t>
    <t s="38">surrounding.</t>
    <t s="39">And the light [intended] to illuminate the worlds,</t>
    <t s="40">even though this light too is attached to the Essence and is of the same kind as the Essence,</t>
    <t s="41">nevertheless, since this light is for the sake of the worlds,</t>
    <t s="42">the worlds occupy a place relative to it,</t>
    <t s="43">and therefore even as it is before the tzimtzum,</t>
    <t s="44">when it is not yet applicable for it to illuminate worlds,</t>
    <t s="45">there is in it, in concealment, measurement and limitation</t>
    <t s="46">(the concealed ten sefiros),</t>
    <t s="47">and after it shines into vessels and worlds,</t>
    <t s="48">it becomes enclothed in them.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section uses the analogy of the soul's faculties to explain the difference between Torah (permeating) and mitzvos (encompassing), and how the blessing on mitzvos reveals the will itself.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And it is explained in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="2">that the analogy for this in the faculties of the soul in man</t>
    <t s="3">("From my flesh I shall perceive G-d")</t>
    <t s="4">is the difference between will and the other faculties.</t>
    <t s="5">For that all the faculties become enclothed in the limbs of the body</t>
    <t s="6">(analogous to the permeating light that becomes enclothed in worlds)</t>
    <t s="7">and the will encompasses all the limbs of the body equally</t>
    <t s="8">(analogous to the encompassing light),</t>
    <t s="9">is,</t>
    <t s="10">because all the faculties,</t>
    <t s="11">even before they become enclothed in the limbs of the body,</t>
    <t s="12">are [a separate] existence</t>
    <t s="13">(outside the soul),</t>
    <t s="14">therefore,</t>
    <t s="15">when they are drawn into the limbs of the body,</t>
    <t s="16">they become enclothed in them.</t>
    <t s="17">And the will,</t>
    <t s="18">is not an existence unto itself; its entire essence is the inclination and drawing of the soul,</t>
    <t s="19">therefore,</t>
    <t s="20">even when it is drawn into the limbs of the body, it does not become enclothed in them, but only encompasses them.</t>
    <t s="21">And the maamar continues,</t>
    <t s="22">that correspondingly in the analogue above,</t>
    <t s="23">it is the difference between Torah and mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="24">For Torah,</t>
    <t s="25">which is the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He</t>
    <t s="26">(an existence, so to speak),</t>
    <t s="27">its drawing down below into the person who studies it is in an internal manner,</t>
    <t s="28">"and Your Torah is within my innards."</t>
    <t s="29">And the mitzvos, which are the Supernal Will,</t>
    <t s="30">the revelation of the Essence,</t>
    <t s="31">their drawing down below into the person who fulfills the mitzvos is in a manner of encompassing and concealment,</t>
    <t s="32">that the light of the mitzvah is not felt in the person.</t>
    <t s="33">For that through the fulfillment of mitzvos refinement is effected in the person,</t>
    <t s="34">which is why one mitzvah brings about another mitzvah,</t>
    <t s="35">is only the effect of the light of the mitzvah,</t>
    <t s="36">but the light itself is not felt in him.</t>
    <t s="37">Analogous to the will in the soul of man,</t>
    <t s="38">for even though the will acts upon the limbs of the body,</t>
    <t s="39">the will itself is not revealed in them.</t>
    <t s="40">And the maamar continues</t>
    <t s="41">[at its conclusion,</t>
    <t s="42">in the section that explains the verse "And now, Israel, what does the L-rd your G-d ask of you,</t>
    <t s="43">do not read 'mah' (what) but rather 'me'ah' (one hundred)],</t>
    <t s="44">that in order for the will of the mitzvos itself to be revealed,</t>
    <t s="45">it is through the blessing over the mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="46">And this is the matter of "a person is obligated to recite one hundred blessings every day,"</t>
    <t s="47">one hundred is in Kesser</t>
    <t s="48">(Will),</t>
    <t s="49">and through the one hundred blessings,</t>
    <t s="50">and particularly through the blessing over the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="51">the will is drawn down in revelation.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section clarifies that the entire purpose of all revelations, even those before the tzimtzum, is for the sake of Torah and Israel.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And it must be understood,</t>
    <t s="2">for seemingly,</t>
    <t s="3">the matter of encompassing and internal explained in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="4">for which the analogy of will and intellect was brought,</t>
    <t s="5">is [about] the permeating light and the encompassing light,</t>
    <t s="6">and what does it have to do here to explain the difference between Torah and mitzvos?</t>
    <t s="7">And one could say the explanation for this, by prefacing that this that creation is for the sake of Torah and for the sake of Israel,</t>
    <t s="8">the intention in this is not only for the creation of the world, but also for all the revelations,</t>
    <t s="9">even for the revelations that are before the tzimtzum,</t>
    <t s="10">and even for the revelation of the light of "without beginning and without end," which is the revelation of the Essence.</t>
    <t s="11">For the purpose in all the revelations is so that through them there will subsequently be the creation of the world</t>
    <t s="12">[and even the revelation that is not to illuminate the worlds, but rather the revelation of the Essence, is because it arose in His will, blessed be He, that the light that pertains to the worlds should be drawn from the light that is above relation to worlds],</t>
    <t s="13">and since the creation of the world is for the sake of Torah and for the sake of Israel,</t>
    <t s="14">it follows that all the revelations are also for the sake of Torah and for the sake of Israel.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
